name: NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
description: Voluntary guidance developed by the National Institute of Standards and Technology to help organizations improve the trustworthiness and manage risks of artificial intelligence systems across GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE functions.
applicability_conditions: Organizations designing, developing, deploying, or using AI systems seeking trustworthy and responsible AI practices

requirements.title: Legal and Regulatory Requirements Identification
requirements.normalized_requirement: Legal and other requirements regarding AI risks are understood, managed, and integrated into organizational policies and procedures.
requirements.implementation_guidance: Maintain an AI regulatory inventory and map legal requirements to organizational policies.

requirements.title: Trustworthy AI Characteristics Integration
requirements.normalized_requirement: Trustworthy characteristics (valid, reliable, safe, secure, resilient, explainable, transparent, privacy-enhanced, and fair) are prioritized and integrated into AI lifecycle processes.
requirements.implementation_guidance: Define trustworthy AI principles in the organizational AI code of conduct and engineering guidelines.

requirements.title: Roles and Responsibilities for AI Risk Management
requirements.normalized_requirement: Roles and responsibilities for AI system design, development, deployment, evaluation, and monitoring are clearly defined, allocated, and communicated.
requirements.implementation_guidance: Establish an AI Governance Committee, define RACI matrices for AI projects, and assign designated AI system owners.

requirements.title: AI Risk Management Policies and Processes
requirements.normalized_requirement: Policies, processes, and procedures are in place, operationalized, and maintained to manage AI risks throughout the lifecycle.
requirements.implementation_guidance: Publish standard operating procedures for AI risk assessment, change management, and incident response.

requirements.title: Context of Use and Business Purpose
requirements.normalized_requirement: The intended purpose, context of use, operational environment, and societal impact of the AI system are formally documented.
requirements.implementation_guidance: Complete an AI System Profile capturing business purpose, target users, deployment environment, and expected benefits.

requirements.title: AI System Architecture and Dependencies
requirements.normalized_requirement: The AI system components, algorithms, foundation models, data pipelines, third-party libraries, and external APIs are identified and mapped.
requirements.implementation_guidance: Maintain architecture diagrams, AI Bills of Materials (AIBOM), and third-party vendor dependency registries.

requirements.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Metrics
requirements.normalized_requirement: Test, evaluation, validation, and verification (TEVV) processes are implemented to measure accuracy, reliability, robustness, fairness, and security.
requirements.implementation_guidance: Define performance benchmarks, run red teaming and adversarial testing, and log model evaluation metrics.

requirements.title: Risk Treatment and Mechanism for Overrides
requirements.normalized_requirement: Mechanisms for human intervention, override, fallback, or safe shutdown (kill-switch) are established and operational.
requirements.applicability: Autonomous, agentic, or high-consequence AI systems
requirements.implementation_guidance: Implement technical kill switches, human approval gates, and fallback operational modes for AI applications.
